Aiy, where do I even start... I've been on these 8 mu since I was a girl. Same dirt, same corners. I know what this land will give me.

My man drives a little truck in town most of the year, only home in the busy weeks. My older boy helps when he's back from the city. The second one's still in school, and my mother-in-law helps when her knees let her. So mostly it's me in the field.

I keep 5 mu in wheat-maize — that's the food and the steady money — and the other 3 mu in cotton, like we've always done on the back piece. Cotton is heavy work but it pays in one lump, and my sister from the next village comes over for picking, we split what we earn.

**Wheat.** I plant around the 10th of October, sometimes a few days later if I'm worn out. I buy seed from the village co-op now — my saved seed doesn't do like it used to. Before plowing I spread one bag of compound on every two mu, that's what I've always done. Then when the wheat greens up in spring I put half a bag of urea per mu. If the leaves still look pale at jointing I'll go heavier — I'd rather waste a bit of fertilizer than look at a yellow field. I run the well three times: after planting, spring greening, filling. If April rains good I skip one, the pump eats money. I hire the sprayer that comes around — ten yuan a mu for weeds and aphids, twice. Combine at harvest, fifty a mu, done in half a day. I figure 400 kg a mu in a normal year, more if the spring rain is kind.

**Maize.** Day the combine leaves my wheat I'm out with the seed. No time to plow — I borrow my cousin's direct-seed planter and pay him back in labor. Hybrid seed, whatever the shop has priced reasonable, around 35 yuan a mu. Compound goes down with the seed, then urea when the maize is knee-high. Water once, twice at most — if July rains you don't need more. We pick the ears by hand in late September, my son-in-law brings his little trailer. I count on 450 kg a mu.

**Cotton.** The hard one. Plant around April 15th when the soil is warm enough. Improved seed costs more, 50 yuan a mu, but the cheap seed won't boll right. Half a bag of compound as base, then urea in June when it starts flowering. Cotton is sprayer-hungry — herbicide once, then two or three times for bollworm and aphids, whatever the village sprayer says is going around. Flood irrigate twice, at flowering and when the bolls are filling. Picking starts in September, three or four rounds, goes till late October. My sister, my mother-in-law, me — and one day-worker if rain is coming and I need to hurry. A good year I get 250 kg lint a mu. Cotton prices have been weak, and if it drops more at harvest I'll think about switching those 3 mu over to wheat-maize next season. But I know cotton, and changing is risky when you've only got 8 mu to live on.
